summary: M11 guard is now truly cell-scoped: one CellQueryTokenGuard per rlm_eval execution captures its baseline at the first admission and compares only the cell's observed positive growth against maxQueryTokensPerCell. A Session already above the ceiling before the cell starts admits that cell's first query (Issue#66 counter-example 1), the accounting resets at every new cell, and onFollowup is now guarded too. Only official token-meter data is used; unobserved child-session spend is never invented.
steps: Verified at 5a1b6e1: enforceQueryTokenGuard compared measure(parent.session).baseline.usage directly against the ceiling, so historical Session pressure could block a fresh cell's first query and a long session could exceed the ceiling before a new cell began.
Rewrote the guard as a cell-scoped observer (lazy baseline + monotonic peak) and moved construction into the shared cell-input factory used by foreground and job paths.
Updated the M11 regression that asserted the buggy behavior (above-ceiling rejection) to the accepted per-cell contract and added growth/reset regressions.

evidence.note: 12/12 pass for the combined guard/job regression set

limitations: The guard observes the parent Session only; per-child subagent spend that the official meter does not aggregate remains unobserved and is documented as a limitation, not estimated.
